title: Make the 'All fetchers cover all 7 curricula' test verify against CurriculumId.values instead of a hand-maintained map
rule: TQ-8 (assertion weaker than what the source can actually do wrong)

evidence.quote:
// All 7 curricula with dedicated fetchers.
      expect(fetchers.length, 7);

why: The test's title claims 'each CurriculumId has a corresponding fetcher' but it only checks internal self-consistency of a hardcoded 7-entry map — it never iterates CurriculumId.values. CurriculumId actually has 9 values; only 'tanach' is registered in CompositeCurriculumStrategy._registry as fetcher-exempt (composite of chumash+nach). 'mishnehTorah' is neither composite nor present in the fetcher map nor backed by any class in tool/lib/sefaria/, yet the test passes regardless — a curriculum can silently lack fetcher coverage forever without this 'coverage' test ever turning red. (Whether mishneh_torah.json is actually correct today is not established here — the defect is that this test cannot detect the gap either way.)
recommendation: Rewrite the test to iterate CurriculumId.values, skip ids where CompositeCurriculumStrategy.isComposite(id.storageKey) is true, and assert every remaining id has a fetcher entry.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails today (before any fetcher is added) if run against the corrected assertion, proving it actually detects the mishnehTorah gap
Test passes once mishnehTorah is either registered composite or given a real fetcher
